items.stem: A user cannot add more columns to a large list around 300 columns. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The 8,000-byte-per-item row size limit has been reached
options.rationale: Correct: column count is bounded by the per-item byte limit, not a fixed column count.
Lists support many columns, subject to the byte limit.

options.text: The list must be deleted and recreated
options.rationale: Recreating does not raise the byte limit.
Teams does not impose a separate column block.

items.explanation: Correct: column count is bounded by the per-item byte limit, not a fixed column count.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about Microsoft Lists? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Lists can be created from built-in templates
options.rationale: Correct: templates such as Issue tracker speed up list creation.

options.text: Lists can be surfaced as a tab in a Teams channel
options.rationale: Correct: the Lists app is available as a Teams tab.
Lists is a tracking app, not cloud storage infrastructure.

options.text: Lists require Bicep to create columns
options.rationale: Columns are created in the UI, not with Bicep.

items.explanation: Correct: templates such as Issue tracker speed up list creation.

items.stem: What keeps a team in sync when a list item's status changes?

options.text: A rule that sends a notification
options.rationale: Correct: rules trigger notifications on changes such as status updates.
Deleting removes the item rather than notifying.
Redundancy is an Azure Storage concept, not a Lists feature.
Peering is an Azure networking concept, unrelated to Lists.
